In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
critical rationality is the only viable alternative to psychiatry's identity crisis.

critical rationality is a method for the systematic and disciplined pursuit of knowledge that is based upon a critical examination of the assumptions of the knowledge being sought, of the methods used to obtain that knowledge, and of the conclusions drawn from that knowledge.
critical rationality is an appropriate and necessary approach for the future of psychiatry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
psychiatry needs to be more rational in its use of the scientific method and more critical of its own practices.

critical rationality requires a disciplined approach to psychiatric knowledge, which underscores the necessity of (a) methodological rigor; (b) practicality; (c) mid-range theorizing; and the necessity of (d) systematic self-critique; (e) reform; (f) self-awareness, including attention to the ethical dimension of psychiatric practice; and (g) attention to the social and political dimensions of psychiatry.
psychiatry must be a critical rational science.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current identity crisis in psychiatry is not a temporary state of affairs.
critical rationality provides a framework for psychiatry's identity that will help the field move beyond its current state of crisis.
psychiatry needs to become a more critical, scientific discipline.
